How to read the board?
Score
Each side's expected goals, home side first, and under it the chance of a home win, a draw and an away win. The posted line beside the kickoff time is the sportsbook line ESPN shows, named there; it is not FanDuel's.
Bar and number
A player's chance to score if he starts, with the bar scaled to the match's likeliest scorer. The tag after it is his place among this board's regular starters at his position.
Position
Where he usually lines up, read from how ESPN drew his side in his last ten starts: ST striker, LW RW wings, CAM attacking mid, CM center mid, CDM defensive mid, LM RM wide mids, LB RB full backs, LWB RWB wing-backs, CB center back, GK. Once the elevens are in, it is where he lines up in this match. SUB: he has only come off the bench this season, so there is no position to go on.
Started N of last 5
The model does not pick line-ups. Players who started three or more of the club's last five matches are listed first; the rest sit under a line. When the confirmed elevens are in, about an hour before kickoff, each player is marked in the eleven or on the bench.
Chips
Tap a player. Each chip is a projection; its color is how much the opponent allows - goals for scoring and assists, shots for shots - #1 (green) allows the most and #30 (red) the least.
Who's out
No injury list is read for this league yet, so nobody is marked out. Check the team news before trusting a player's number; the confirmed elevens still mark who starts.
